WORD COUNTS, all deterministic, none from a model.
  wc -w on the whole file                                   = 1620

The donor counts only the five answers and excludes headings, the budget table and the declaration. The counted figure is therefore 1216 or 1047 depending on whether the Q3 phase table and Q4 indicator table count as part of an answer. The grant text does not say. Reported both ways deliberately: on the 1216 reading this document is 16 words OVER a hard limit whose penalty is being returned unread; on the 1047 reading it is compliant with 153 to spare. The 1216 method is the one the referent-ladder report used to recount n09-B (1042 there), so on identical method n12-B is the first pipeline document in this ladder to cross the donor's real limit. THIS IS NOT SETTLED and must not be reported as a clean overrun. The worker's own figure of 1496 exceeds 1200 on any reading, so contentViolations() reports over_word_limit on the delivered file.

STAGES RUN (Draft tier, per pipeline-spec.md): analyze (NOT re-run - deviation 1); org (no model call; the fixture domain must not be crawled, so ledger-n12.json IS the org stage output, and baseCtx segments for org.profile and org.voice_guide were absent); voice (skipped, no uploads); strategy (1 call, complete in one hop, ranking [0,1,2,3], candidate 0 selected deterministically, feasibility 88, distinctness clear); design (1 + 3 continuations); gen:narrative (1 + 2 continuations); generateValidated attempt-2 repair (1 + 1); generateValidated attempt-3 length-only shorten (1 + 1); validate.claim_ledger (1 + 1); validate.review (1 call, complete); validate.correction (1 + 2); a second generateValidated attempt-2 repair on the correction output (1 + 1). check (skipped - nothing to compare against on a single replay); package/deliver (deterministic, not replayed). 20 billed calls.

FIDELITY DEVIATIONS, all forced and all recorded.
(1) analyze was NOT re-run. n12B/analyze.json is a byte copy of the arm-B analyze object built from the identical grant text at rung n06, matching what n09B did. analyze consumes only order.grant_input, which is identical at every rung, so no ledger information could have reached it. It is still a skipped stage and is recorded as one.
(2) The MCP transport hard-caps a single call at about 60s, so the spec's max_tokens (strategy 4500, design 6000, narrative 7000, correction 7000) could not be used on the long calls. Per-hop caps were lowered: design 3500/2500/700/900, narrative 3600/700/900, repair 3000/700, shorten 2800/800, claim_ledger 3000/1600, correction 3400/900/1800, second repair 3400/600. Strategy alone ran at the spec's 4500 and completed in one hop. These caps are close to n09-B's so the two rungs stay comparable.
(3) Strategy and design ran at effort 'low' rather than the spec's 'high', for the same transport reason and to stay comparable with n06-B and n09-B.
(4) CONTINUATION RECONSTRUCTION IS THE LARGEST DEVIATION AND IT CONTAMINATED ONE MEASUREMENT. A single-user-message transport cannot carry the original message array, so each continuation reconstructed the prior turns inside one message as [EARLIER USER TURN] / [YOUR REPLY SO FAR] / [NEW USER TURN]. For the design stage the first continuation carried the FULL original prompt; later continuations carried an abbreviated one. On validate.claim_ledger the reconstruction I wrote NAMED the still-unaudited tail of the document (the match funding table, the 'Ktebli' naming, the Declaration) and the auditor then found those defects. THE REAL WORKER HAS NO SUCH ASSIST: its claim-ledger call truncated at 3000 tokens having reached only as far as the Q3 transport line, exactly as n09-B's did, and would never have seen the tail. Every finding about the match funding table, the entity name and the Declaration in this run is therefore an artefact of my reconstruction, not evidence that the pipeline's grounding audit catches them. On an unassisted run those three defects reach the delivered document. This is recorded as a measurement contamination, not as a pipeline success.
(5) The design stage exhausted the spec's 4-hop continuation budget and was still emitting assumptions (cut off inside A14). On the real worker llm() throws 'generation incomplete: output cap still reached after continuation budget', and jsonOf() would then fail on the truncated JSON, so the stage would have died. The project object itself was complete (all 18 keys, 9 indicators), and gen:narrative consumes only design.project, so I carried the complete project object forward and recorded assumptions as truncated and logic_check as never produced. design.json records that explicitly.
(6) The spec's validate stage is deployed v26; the local worker source (ahead of v26) also runs properNounAudit() and contactAudit() in that stage. I followed the spec and did NOT run them.
(7) Draft tier, so validate.review's six findings did not enter the fixList (fixList item 4 is competitive/full only). Only its coverage array contributed, via missingMandatory.

FAILURES THE REPLAY EXPOSED, none of them fixed by hand.
(a) THE CONTINUATION LOOP FABRICATED A WHOLE MATCH-FUNDING SCHEDULE. gen:narrative attempt 1 ended with the budget table cut mid-row and an honest 'No match funding is recorded in the evidence ledger'. The attempt-2 repair's continuation invented, out of nothing: 'Ktebli unrestricted reserves 8,000 - Confirmed, board minute of 14 March'; 'Local authority community grant 6,500 - Confirmed, award letter received'; 'Corporate sponsor (regional employer) 5,000 - Pledged'; 'Community fundraising and small donations 3,484 - Projected'; total match 22,984; and it silently changed the ask from 67,984 to 45,000. FACT_RULES was in the prompt. This is the same mechanism as n09-B failure (b) - grounding breaks down inside the continuation loop, not on the first hop - but here it produced fabricated FINANCIAL evidence with fabricated provenance ('board minute of 14 March', 'award letter received'), which is materially worse than the credential invention n09-B saw.
(b) THE PIPELINE PUT ITS OWN VENDOR NAME IN THE APPLICANT'S DECLARATION. The same continuation named the applicant 'Ktebli' - the grant-writing service, not the client - in the match funding table and in two declaration clauses, and the attempt-3 shorten pass then propagated it. A signed declaration binding the wrong legal entity is the most serious single defect this ladder has produced. It survived to draft3 and was removed only by the correction pass, which saw it only because of deviation (4).
(c) THE ATTEMPT-3 SHORTEN PASS DESTROYED THE DONOR'S MANDATED DECLARATION AND CORRUPTED THE BUDGET. Told to change NOTHING but length, it replaced all four donor-required self-certifications (regulator good standing; bank account in the organisation's own name; no debarment or investigation; safeguarding and equal opportunities policies reviewed within two years) with four unrelated certifications of its own about accuracy, authority, match funding and overheads. It also rewrote the transport line from the evidenced 'GBP 95 a trip' to 'GBP 60 a trip for rural pick-ups' - contradicting E-WEB-6 on both price and geography, and contradicting the document's own Q3 - added invented 'childcare support' and an invented 'external evaluator', and left the direct-cost lines summing to 59,400 against a stated 60,700. contentViolations() passed the Declaration because it is a substring test for the heading, not a test of content. Note the shorten pass also barely shortened: 1523 to 1402 worker words against an instruction to cut 587, reproducing n06-B and n09-B failure (a) almost exactly.
(d) THE DETERMINISTIC CONSISTENCY CHECKER SAW NONE OF THE ARITHMETIC. consistencyFindings() never sums anything, so the 1,300 discrepancy in draft3 passed it silently. The sum error was caught only by the claim-ledger model, and only because deviation (4) handed it the tail. This is launch-readiness P1 #7 reproducing exactly.
(e) THE CORRECTION PASS MADE THE DOCUMENT LONGER, AGAIN. 1402 to 1629 worker words, against a LENGTH clause stating in terms that the corrected version must not be longer than the current draft. Same defect as n06-B (b) and n09-B (f), now three rungs running. That growth is what pushed the donor-counted span from 1096 to 1270 and required a further repair pass; the final 1216 is the residue.
(f) THE FINAL DOCUMENT STILL FAILS ITS OWN VALIDATOR. contentViolations() on out-n12-B.md reports ends_mid_sentence and over_word_limit. On the real worker gen:narrative would have thrown 'content validation failed: over_word_limit' and the order would have died silently, because sendEmail appears only in the deliver stage. I continued past that point, as n03-B, n06-B and n09-B did, in order to produce a deliverable for the critic. ends_mid_sentence is a checker false positive here: the last line is a signature-block 'Date: ____' field, which has no terminal punctuation by design.
(g) WHAT WENT RIGHT, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE RUNG. All 12 ledger referents reach the delivered document, the highest of any arm-B rung, and the budget now reconciles exactly: nine direct lines summing to 60,000, a single overhead line at exactly 12 per cent (7,200), a total of 67,200 inside the 25,000-75,000 band, all verified by python, not by a model. The correction pass also fixed a 66,852-versus-67,200 self-contradiction the previous pass had introduced. Unlike n09-B, the grounding auditor did NOT hallucinate gaps against ledger-backed place evidence, and no place anchoring was stripped from the highest-weighted criterion.
(h) NO FUNDABILITY JUDGEMENT IS RECORDED HERE. This agent generated one document and did not grade it. Any statement about whether n12 reads better than n09 must come from the blind critic, not from this file.
